note: Adapted from the species description in Sands (1972), originally in English. The genus has no soldiers, hence there is no soldier section; measurement tables, figure numbers and locality records are not translated, and the characters of the genus Alyscotermes given later on the same page are not used.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Comparisons with the other species of the genus have been made in their respective descriptions. The present species, whose distinction from the closely related genera is the clearest, is the least likely to be merged should the limits of the genus require adjustment in future, and has therefore been designated the type species of the genus. The worker abdomen is at least potentially dehiscent.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule pale yellow; pilosity yellow, sparse and long. Postclypeus moderately inflated, Pcl/W 0.29–0.31, Pcl/Rj 2.38–2.60. Mandibular apical tooth rather long, La/Ly 0.71–0.79, Ra/Ri 1.00–1.02; a distinct notch separates the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible from the molar prominence in surface view, La/Li·Lm 11.40–12.55; the apical and marginal teeth are nearly in line, the anterior margin of the first marginal tooth distinctly longer than that of the second, Ra/Ri·Rm 14.49–14.80. Fore tibia scarcely inflated, Ti/Tw 5.33–5.42; third apical spur distinct, about half the length of the other two spurs. The overlapping part of the midgut–hindgut junction is oblique and lies to the right of the Malpighian tubule knot; in the unopened abdomen the enteric valve seat is lateral, very weakly trilobed, and joined to the second hindgut pouch by a short neck; the valve membrane bears sparse minute spines outside the cushions.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule brown to dark brown, darker above the ocelli, the dark area usually extending as tapering stripes that converge on the fontanelle; fontanelle rather large, slightly smaller than the ocellus, circular or slightly broader than long, its outline sometimes irregular, flat or slightly concave, yellowish white to pale yellowish brown; central spot circular, flat, smaller than the fontanelle, brown; postclypeus yellowish brown, labrum yellow; frontal groove weakly developed, a flat crescent, pale yellowish brown to brown; antennae yellow to pale yellowish brown. Pronotum and meso- and metanotum brown, transverse sutures distinct; femora yellowish brown, tibiae paler, tarsi yellow. Abdominal tergites brown, dorsal spiracles and sternites pale brown, the median part of the sternites paler, ventral spiracles pale; cerci yellow. Posterior margin of head capsule usually even but slightly broadly rounded; ocelli moderate, their distance from the compound eye about equal to their minimum diameter; postclypeus weakly to moderately inflated, Pcl/W 0.23–0.27, posterior margin arcuate, median suture distinct. Mandibular apical tooth rather long, La/L1 0.68–0.78, Ra/Rj 0.92–1.06; a distinct notch separates the subsidiary tooth of the left mandible from the molar prominence in surface view, La/L1·Lm 6.34–8.90; the tips of the apical and marginal teeth of the right mandible are in line, and the anterior margin of the first marginal tooth is slightly longer than that of the second. Meso- and metanotum of moderate width at the constriction, M/W 0.32–0.35. Cephalic pilosity yellowish brown, a rather sparse and slightly uneven layer, with outstanding setae.
